title: HyHO-DDI: A Hypergraph Neural Network for High-Order Drug-Drug Interaction Prediction
items.abstract: <jats:p>Objective: Drug–drug interactions (DDIs) are a major cause of adverse drug reactions (ADRs), particularly in patients receiving multiple medications. Existing computational methods predominantly focus on pairwise interactions, limiting their ability to capture the complex effects of high-order (multi-drug) therapies. This study proposes a computational framework for predicting myopathy-associated high-order DDIs.Methods: We propose HyHO-DDIs, a hypergraph neural network model for predicting myopathy-associated high-order drug combinations using a dataset curated from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). In our model, each drug is represented by molecular fingerprint features and a protein-target profile, and we construct a hypergraph in which nodes are drugs and hyperedges correspond to multi-drug combinations implicated in myopathy. The model integrates Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) layers with hypergraph-based attention to learn high-order interaction representations, and a decoder outputs the predicted risk of myopathy for an input drug combination. We evaluated HyHO-DDI with 5-fold cross-validation and compared it against an MLP with the same inputs, as well as established high-order baselines (HODDI, D3I).Results: HyHO-DDI consistently achieved higher performance across F1-score, AUROC, and AUC-PR. The proposed model reduced false-positive predictions while maintaining strong performance on previously unseen drug combinations, demonstrating robust generalization.Conclusion: HyHO-DDI provides an effective framework for predicting myopathy-associated high-order DDIs by explicitly modeling multi-drug interactions with hypergraphs. The proposed approach has the potential to improve computational pharmacovigilance by prioritizing potentially hazardous drug combinations and supporting medication safety.</jats:p>

title: Prediction of Supercritical CO₂ Solubility with a Thermodynamics-Conditioned Equivariant Graph Neural Network Model
items.abstract: <jats:p>Supercritical CO₂ (scCO₂) is a green alternative to organic solvents and the working fluid of supercritical fluid extraction (SFE), used in analytical sample preparation and natural-product isolation. Its wider adoption is limited by the difficulty of predicting analyte solubility: experimental determination at supercritical conditions is tedious, requires specialized equipment, and yields values that vary by up to two orders of magnitude across laboratories. Existing predictive models either rely on substance-specific fitted parameters or trade mechanistic transparency for accuracy. We present an interpretable graph-neural-network framework that couples the equivariant Polarizable Atom Interaction Neural Network (PaiNN) with Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), integrating global thermodynamic descriptors (temperature, pressure, density, evaporation enthalpy, critical point) into a three-dimensional structure-aware model. It was trained on 27,461 solubility measurements across 958 organic molecules curated from Makarov et al., 2025. Five-fold cross-validation gave a coefficient of determination of 0.767 and a median absolute deviation of 0.36 in log₁₀-solubility, with stable per-fold performance (R² = 0.767 ± 0.048) and confirmation on an external dataset. To verify the model reasons chemically, we adapted a walk-based GNN layer-wise relevance propagation explainer to the FiLM architecture and added structural ablation. Atom-rank consistency across folds (ρ = 0.72), plausible element rankings (O, N > C, H), and trends with molecular weight, polar surface area and acetylation show that predictions rest on physically meaningful patterns. The ready-to-use model enables in silico SFE screening and reduces organic-solvent use in sample preparation.</jats:p>
